'''Roxanne L. Johnson''' is an American [[chemist]] specialized in developing and applying [[Quantitative Methods|quantitative methods]] to determine nutrients, organic and [[Inorganic carbon compound|inorganic carbon]] and [[total suspended solids]] in [[estuarine]] seawater systems. She works for the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency]].

== Education ==
Johnson completed a B.A. in chemical science at [[Connecticut College]] in 1965. In 1997, she earned a M.S. in statistics at the [[University of Rhode Island]] (URI).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Johnson|first=Roxanne|date=November 2016|title=Curriculum Vitae|url=https://19january2017snapshot.epa.gov/sites/production/files/2016-11/documents/johnson_roxanne.pdf|access-date=2020-07-18|website=U.S. Environmental Protection Agency}}{{PD-notice}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
From 1978 to 1982, Johnson was a research assistant in the URI biochemistry department. She was a marine research specialist at URI working for the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency]] (EPA) from 1982 to 1988. She worked as an associate chemist for the [[Science Applications International Corporation]] on contract with the EPA from 1988 to 1995. In 1995, Johnson joined the Atlantic Ecology Division of the EPA's National Health and Environmental Effects Research Laboratory.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=US EPA|first=OEAEE|title=Staff Details|url=https://cfpub.epa.gov/locator/in_details.cfm?LAST_NAME=Johnson&FIRST_NAME=Roxanne&MAIL_CD=&SITE_CD=LAB&SITE_DESC=LABORATORIES&search=1&sort=1&ASSOC_PK=16228&tab=search|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200719023041/https://cfpub.epa.gov/locator/in_details.cfm?LAST_NAME=Johnson&FIRST_NAME=Roxanne&MAIL_CD=&SITE_CD=LAB&SITE_DESC=LABORATORIES&search=1&sort=1&ASSOC_PK=16228&tab=search|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 19, 2020|access-date=2020-07-19|website=cfpub.epa.gov|language=en}}</ref>

Johnson develops and applies [[Quantitative Methods|quantitative methods]] to determine nutrients, organic and [[Inorganic carbon compound|inorganic carbon]] and [[total suspended solids]] in [[estuarine]] seawater systems. She has developed and applied [[experimental designs]] and [[statistical analyses]], using Primer and [[SAS (software)|SAS]], to the study of [[Benthic zone|benthic]] communities as indicators of estuarine health in several [[New England]] estuarine systems.<ref name=":0" />
